run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T08:01:48Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend RequestErrorRate alert is explained by frontend's checkout calls failing, not by a fault inside frontend itself. Frontend error spans were 0 at the 08:01 sample and rose from 08:02 onward, confined to POST /api/checkout, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout', the client span grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and tcp.connect; frontend's cart, ad and product-catalog calls show no error spans in the window. The dependency checkout is down: pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q is not ready, CrashLoopBackOff, restartCount 11, last termination reason Error/exitCode 2 at 08:07:41, its live container spec carries gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest for both the checkout container and the wait-for-kafka init container although the Deployment checkout template still specifies ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout; Deployment checkout reports unavailableReplicas 1 and Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable) since 08:07:41, and Service checkout has only a notReadyAddress, so no ready endpoint exists. Chaos-mesh events record Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay (namespace chaos-mesh) spawning PodChaos objects every minute from 08:00:41 to 08:09:41, each recording 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q', with kubelet events 'Container checkout definition changed, will be restarted' (08:03:41), pause image already present (08:07:08) and 'Back-off restarting failed container checkout' (08:08:29). That Schedule/PodChaos chain is the object identified from events as applying the change; the exact PodChaos action is inferred from the pause image in the pod spec and the chaos-mesh custom resources could not be read, so the conclusion is partial. All other otel-demo pods, including frontend-675fd7b5c5-gc9hg, are Running, ready with 0 restarts.

claims.text: Frontend error spans (sum of increase over 5m of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend"} with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR) were 0 at the 08:01 sample, 74.44 at 08:02, reached a plateau of about 216-228 per 5m from 08:08 to 08:12 and were 61.27 at 08:16; the alert started at 08:01:48.

The frontend error spans are specifically POST /api/checkout (16.67 per 5m at 08:02, 216.67 at 08:08), executing api route (pages) /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (same counts) and tcp.connect (7.78 per 5m at 08:02 up to 16.67), while the frontend error series for grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, CartService/AddItem, AdService/GetAds, ProductCatalog GetProduct, GET /api/cart and GET /api/data are all 0 for the whole queried window.

frontend-proxy error spans on the operations 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' rose at the same time as the frontend checkout errors, from roughly 1-4 per 5m before 08:02 to about 227-230 per 5m between 08:08 and 08:12.
For the frontend POST operation, error spans went from 0 at 08:01 to 216.67 per 5m against 614.44 UNSET spans at 08:08, and were still 61.27 at 08:16.

Pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q in namespace otel-demo has spec container 'checkout' with image gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest and init container 'wait-for-kafka' with the same pause image, while its containerStatuses image is ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout; it is ready=false, restartCount=11, state.waiting.reason=CrashLoopBackOff, lastState.terminated.reason=Error, exitCode=2, finishedAt 2026-11-17T08:07:41Z (startedAt 08:07:36Z).

Deployment checkout in namespace otel-demo has spec.replicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1, and condition Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable and lastTransitionTime 2026-11-17T08:07:41Z, while its pod template still specifies image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout, so no template change explains the pod's pause image.

Service checkout selects opentelemetry.io/name=checkout and exposes port 8080, and its Endpoints object lists only notReadyAddresses for pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q (IP 100.96.4.26) with no ready addresses.

Chaos-mesh events show Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay (namespace chaos-mesh) with reason Spawned creating PodChaos objects otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay-zv9mn, -927gn, -d2m7w, -dc4vz, -jgn2n, -ktl9k, -vxxwz, -6cwbh, -qgddz and -gl228 between 08:00:41Z and 08:09:41Z, each PodChaos recording 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q' and, for nine of them, TimeUp/Recovered about 55 seconds later; kubelet events for the same pod record 'Container checkout definition changed, will be restarted' at 08:03:41Z, 'Container image gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest already present on machine' at 08:07:08Z and 'Back-off restarting failed container checkout' at 08:08:29Z.

The object that applied the change to the failing pods is Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay in namespace chaos-mesh, whose spawned PodChaos records name otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q as the target it applied chaos to repeatedly through the incident window.

Checkout's own span volume (increase over 5m of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout"}) was about 2,700-3,000 per 5m before the incident, fell to 1,982 at 08:03 and 871 at 08:05, and was 0 from 08:07 onward.

Among the 21 pods in namespace otel-demo, checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q is the only one not ready (Running, ready=false, CrashLoopBackOff); every other pod, including frontend-675fd7b5c5-gc9hg, frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-c8ks2, product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-q8nt8, cart-755465879b-7khmf, payment-55766d76b9-rlrgr and email-59f69bc6cf-zsfdz, is Running, ready=true with 0 restarts.

The failing pod belongs to ReplicaSet checkout-5dccddf8bb, whose ownerReference is Deployment checkout, and the pod's startTime is 2026-11-17T07:23:59Z, before the 08:00 chaos onset, so it was not newly created by a rollout during the incident.

The checkout container's readable current-instance logs end at 2026-11-17T07:46:50Z and the newest 80 lines are successful PlaceOrder/payment/email/'order placed' messages with no error text; the previous container instance's logs were reported unavailable.

Error spans on the ad, fraud-detection and recommendation services (flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream, ResolveInt) were already present at a steady ~1.1 per 5m before 08:00 and across the incident window, so they are pre-existing background and not tied to the alert's deviation at 08:01.

A product-catalog network delay (suggested only by the chaos object's name otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay) is not supported as this cause: product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-q8nt8 is Running and ready with 0 restarts, no product-catalog error-span series appears in the window, and the injected pod's own spec holds the pause image with the failures confined to checkout availability.

The repeated PodChaos injections spawned by Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay (pause-image patches applied at least once a minute from 08:00:41) restarted and ultimately left the checkout pod unable to serve, removing checkout's only ready endpoint and producing the frontend POST /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder errors behind the RequestErrorRate alert.

The checkout container's last termination (reason Error, exitCode 2, 08:07:36-08:07:41) may include an application-level startup failure in addition to the chaos restarts; the available logs cannot separate these two possibilities.

Inspect the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay and the PodChaos objects it spawns (the events name otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q as the applied target) and stop the experiment if it is not intended; its name says product-catalog network delay while the evidence shows a pause-image restart of checkout.

After the chaos is removed, recreate pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q so the ReplicaSet re-applies the Deployment template image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout instead of gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest, then verify the pod is ready, that Service checkout has a ready endpoint, and that frontend POST /api/checkout error spans return to zero.

gaps: The chaos-mesh custom resources (Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay and its PodChaos objects) are not readable with the available Kubernetes kinds, so their spec/status and exact action (pod-failure versus another action) are known only from events and from the pause image observed in the pod spec.

Jaeger returned no traces for frontend in the incident window (traces_search and traces_search_by_tags returned no_data): the newest traces found are from 2026-11-17T07:54:43-07:54:44Z with HTTP 200, so status codes and error messages of the failing POST /api/checkout spans during 08:00-08:19 could not be read.
The checkout container's previous-instance logs were unavailable (no previous instance) and its current-instance logs end at 07:46:50Z, so nothing in the logs explains the exit code 2 at 08:07:41Z.
The frontend pod's logs returned 0 lines for the whole window, so the frontend-side error messages for the failing checkout calls are unverified.

A query for kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="otel-demo"} returned no series, so Deployment availability over time is not measured; the deployment state reported above is API state at query time, after the incident window.

list_prometheus_rules returned no rule named RequestErrorRate and no alerting rules at all, so the alert expression, its window and the reported 3.4999999999999996 value could not be verified against the rule definition.
No PodChaos target labels or selector could be read, so which other pods the experiment may have targeted (beyond the events naming checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q) is unknown.
Change history and Alertmanager integrations are not available in this Run, so who or what created the chaos Schedule could not be checked.
next_steps: Read the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay and the PodChaos objects it spawned directly to confirm action, duration, target selector and whether it is still active.

After the chaos is stopped, confirm the checkout pod's live spec matches the Deployment template and that Service checkout has a ready endpoint, then watch frontend /api/checkout error spans and the RequestErrorRate alert clear.

Check the checkout application's startup path (or the node's container log files for the previous instance) to confirm whether exit code 2 is caused only by the chaos restarts or by an application error.
